cards.explanation: The answer is False. The ten do meet Jesus, but they stood at a distance (Luke 17:12). Nobody walks up for a handshake. It's a meeting where everybody stays at the back of the room and the front row sits empty.

The answer is that they raise their voices and shout. Luke says they “raised their voices, shouting, ‘Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!’” (Luke 17:13). No messenger, no middleman. Just ten voices doing the job themselves, friends, and that's a lot of lung power for one road.

The answer is mercy. They shout, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!” (Luke 17:13). They don't hand Him a long list, friends. It's one short request, and they shout it loud enough to reach Him from where they stand.

The answer is to go show themselves to the priests. Jesus tells them, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” (Luke 17:14). He doesn't say come over here first, bakers. He gives them a direction and nothing more. I'd have wanted a map and a cookie for the road.

The answer is True. Luke says, “…as they were on their way, they were cleansed.” (Luke 17:14). They haven't reached the priests yet, friends. The cleansing shows up mid-walk, like pulling a batch out of the oven and finding the timer still has minutes left.

The answer is that he comes back to Jesus. When he saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God (Luke 17:15). Everybody had been walking one way, and he turns around. That's a U-turn, friends, and I bet there's a whole lot of joy behind it.
The answer is True. He came back, “…praising God in a loud voice.” (Luke 17:15). That's no whisper and no polite little nod, bakers. This man has no indoor voice, and I love it.

The answer is False. The ten stood at a distance in the beginning (Luke 17:12). But this man falls facedown at Jesus' feet in thanksgiving (Luke 17:16). He goes from a long-distance shout to as close as it gets, friends.
The answer is a Samaritan. Luke says, “…and he was a Samaritan.” (Luke 17:16). Later Jesus calls him “this foreigner” (Luke 17:18). So the one who came back, friends, is the Samaritan.

The answer is that Jesus asks where the other nine are. He asks, “Were not all ten cleansed?” and then, “Where then are the other nine?” (Luke 17:17). The count is right there in His words, bakers. Ten were cleansed, and one is at His feet.

The answer is glory. Jesus asks, “Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?” (Luke 17:18). The man had been praising God in a loud voice (Luke 17:15). That's giving glory, friends, and Jesus puts a name on it.

The answer is faith. Jesus tells him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!” (Luke 17:19). That's the last thing Jesus says to this man in the passage, friends. He came back and fell facedown at Jesus' feet (Luke 17:15-16), and those are the words Jesus gives him.
